links.comparator_used: Radiologist interpretation of all LDCT examinations without AI
links.outcome: Recall rate, per-examination specificity, per-nodule sensitivity, mean interpretation time and net benefit on decision-curve analysis
links.effect: AI as prescreener vs no AI: recall 20.8% vs 22.1% (p=.02); mean interpretation time 143 vs 164 seconds (p=.001); per-examination specificity 90.3% vs 88.8% (p=.04); per-nodule sensitivity 62.9% vs 64.2% (p=.16, not significant). Only the prescreener scenario showed higher net benefit than interpretation without AI.
links.tradeoff: Per-nodule sensitivity was numerically lower (62.9% vs 64.2%), though not significantly. Radiologists read only AI-positive examinations, so any nodule the AI misses is not reviewed.
links.quote: Among scenarios, only AI as a prescreener demonstrated higher net benefit than interpretation without AI; AI as an assistant had the least net benefit.
